# 2 Chronicles Chapter 31 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** When the festival was over, all the Israelites who had attended went out to the towns of Judah and smashed the sacred stones, cut down the Asherah poles, and demolished the high places and altars throughout Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh until they had destroyed them all. Then all the Israelites returned to their own towns and property.

**2** Hezekiah assigned the priests and Levites to divisions, each with specific duties — offering burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, serving, giving thanks, and singing praises at the gates of the LORD's residence.

**3** The king contributed from his own possessions for the morning and evening burnt offerings and for the burnt offerings on Sabbaths, New Moons, and the appointed festivals, as required by the Law of the LORD.

**4** He ordered the people living in Jerusalem to give the portion due to the priests and Levites, so they could devote themselves fully to the Law of the LORD.

**5** As soon as the order went out, the Israelites responded generously with the firstfruits of their grain, new wine, olive oil, honey, and everything their fields produced. They brought a large tithe of everything.

**6** The people of Israel and Judah living in Judah's towns also brought tithes of their herds and flocks, as well as tithes of the holy things dedicated to the LORD their God, piling them in heaps.

**7** They began making the heaps in the third month and finished in the seventh month.

**8** When Hezekiah and his officials came and saw the heaps, they praised the LORD and blessed His people Israel.

**9** Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the heaps.

**10** Azariah the chief priest, from the family of Zadok, answered, "Since the people began bringing their contributions to the LORD's temple, we have had enough to eat and plenty to spare, because the LORD has blessed His people, and this great pile is what's left over."

**11** Hezekiah ordered storerooms to be prepared in the LORD's temple, and this was done.

**12** Then the contributions, tithes, and dedicated gifts were faithfully brought in. The Levite Conaniah was in charge, with his brother Shimei as his assistant.

**13** Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah served as supervisors under Conaniah and Shimei, appointed by King Hezekiah and Azariah, the official in charge of God's temple.

**14** Kore son of Imnah the Levite, the gatekeeper at the East Gate, was in charge of the freewill offerings given to God, distributing the contributions reserved for the LORD and the most sacred offerings.

**15** Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah faithfully assisted him in the towns of the priests, distributing to their priestly relatives by divisions, regardless of age.

**16** In addition, distribution was made to all males three years old or older who were listed in the genealogical records — to all who would enter the LORD's temple for daily duties according to their responsibilities and assignments by divisions.

**17** The priests were registered by families, and the Levites twenty years old and older by their responsibilities and divisions.

**18** They were registered together with all their dependents — wives, sons, and daughters — the whole community, because they faithfully consecrated themselves.

**19** For the descendants of Aaron, the priests living on the farmlands around their towns, men were designated by name in each town to distribute portions to every male among the priests and to every registered Levite.

**20** This is what Hezekiah did throughout Judah. He did what was good, right, and faithful before the LORD his God.

**21** In everything he undertook — in the service of God's temple, in obedience to the law and commands — he sought his God wholeheartedly. And he prospered.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **31:1**: The people don't wait for a royal decree — they go out on their own and tear down the idols. This is what genuine revival looks like: the people own it, not just the king.

- **31:4**: Hezekiah understood that pastors need to eat. If you want the priests and Levites to devote themselves to God's word, you need to pay them. Spiritual leadership is a full-time job.

- **31:10**: "We have enough and plenty left over" — the surplus is the point. When God's people give generously, there isn't just enough. There's more than enough. The heaps are theology made visible.

- **31:21**: "He sought his God wholeheartedly. And he prospered." The Chronicler's most complete endorsement. Hezekiah is the king the Chronicler wishes every king had been.


— PNEUMA
